summary: Mark Teeuwen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. He completed his MA and PhD at Leiden University (~1984–1996) before serving as a lecturer at Cardiff University (1994–1999) and becoming a professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.
Mark Wilks was a historian and Indologist. He served as Resident in the Kingdom of Mysore (~1803–1808) and later as Governor for the Government of Saint Helena (~1813–1816).

Markus Gabriel is a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn (~1999–2002). He held posts at Bonn (~2009), The New School (~2012–2013), UC Berkeley (~2020), and became Global Senior Advisor at the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy in 2024.

Markus Viehbeck is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard (-2012), worked as a Heidelberg University project researcher, and joined Vienna's faculty (attested 2026).

Marsha Weidner is a scholar of Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies. After earning her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, she served at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and as Professor of the History of Art at the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

Marshall Sahlins was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1947–1952) and Columbia University (~1952–1954), held a post at Michigan (~1957–1973), and joined the University of Chicago faculty in 1973.

Marta Sernesi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Turin (-2007) and held an appointment as Gastprofessorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Martha Ann Selby is an Indologist who served as Series Editor for South Asia Research (attested 2014). She is Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin and Sangam Professor and Department Chair at Harvard University (attested 2026).

Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher who studied at Wellesley, NYU, and Harvard, also studying under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Harvard, Oxford, and Brown, before becoming Ernst Freund Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Martin Baumann is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leibniz University Hannover (~1989–1993) and habilitation at the University of Leipzig (~1994–1999), becoming Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

Martin Brauen is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at the Universities of Delhi and Zurich. He held curatorial and leadership posts at the University of Zurich's Ethnographic Museum (1975) and the Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

Martin Collcutt is a scholar of Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and Harvard (PhD 1975), taught in Japan (1963–1969), and served as Director of Princeton University's East Asian Studies Program during his tenure there (1975–2015).

Martin Delhey is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and earned his PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg (-2002). He has held posts at Hamburg, Göttingen, Ryukoku, Shandong, and IIBS.

Martin Haug was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey. He taught at Bonn and Deccan College before becoming Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Munich in 1868.

Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Rickert and Edmund Husserl (~1909–1923). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (1915–1923, 1936–1940) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

Martin Joachim Kümmel is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian-Central Asian studies scholar. He earned his degrees at the University of Freiburg, where he was an Assistent and Akademischer Rat (~1999–2007), before becoming a chair holder at the University of Jena (2013).

Martin King Whyte is a Sinologist and sociologist educated at Cornell and Harvard (PhD 1971). He held faculty posts at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University, and Harvard University, where he became professor emeritus.

Martin Lehnert is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Freiburg and served as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich (attested 2016).

Martin Lowenthal is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen, Humboldt, Heidelberg (PhD), and Munich (Habilitation). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (1990–2011) and at the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (2013).
